newsitem.title: USA: News Corp. to buy Heritage Media.
newsitem.headline: News Corp. to buy Heritage Media.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. Ltd said on Monday it reached an agreement to buy marketing company Heritage Media Corp. for stock valued at about $754 million.
It said it also will assume Heritage's outstanding debt of about $600 million.

News Corp. said it planned to sell Heritage's six network-affiliated television stations and 24 radio stations, while keeping Heritage's marketing services operations that complement those of its own.
Heritage, based in Dallas, provides in-store marketing products and services for grocery, drug and mass merchandise outlets.
"Heritage's marketing services operations are a great complement to our existing FSI (free standing inserts) business," media tycoon Murdoch said said in a statement.
However, New Corp stock sagged as investors questioned the company's $1.35 billion stock-and-debt deal to buy Heritage.
News Corp American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) fell 37.5 cents to close at $20.50 on the New York Stock Exchange. Heritage Media jumped $5.785 to $18 in heavy trade, also on the NYSE.
News Corp. said it was making the acquisition through a subsidiary and would pay the equivalent of $20.50 for each of Heritage's 38.6 million shares.
The transaction is subject to the approvals of the Heritage shareholders and regulatory agencies.

Heritage owns ACTMEDIA Inc., which provides in-store marketing products in more than 40,000 supermarkets, drug stores and mass merchandisers worldwide, and DIMAC Marketing Corp., a full-service, vertically integrated direct marketing services company.

News Corp., through its U.S. division, News America FSI, publishes free-standing promotional inserts in the United States. It produces more than 60 million weekly inserts, which are distributed in more than 600 Sunday newspapers throughout the country.

Analysts said the acquisition of such Heritage units as ACTMEDIA, which provide products like coupons to drug stores and supermarkets, were a good fit for News Corp's free-standing inserts (FSI) business.
However, they questioned Murdoch's further investment in inserts and the effect News Corp's continuing buying spree would have on its balance sheet.

In the last year or so News Corp has spent about $5 billion on purchases, including the $2.8 billion acquisition of New World Communications Group Inc. Most of the purchases have been paid for with stock.
"Strategically it's good; from an earnings standpoint it's good," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales at NatWest Securities.
"The problem is Murdoch spending $1.3 billion," Melinek said. "... It's back to more spending and that has disappointed the market."
Richard Read, an analyst with Arnhold & Bleichroeder, said, "My reaction is that I would rather see the investment elsewhere than FSI and related areas."
Added Ed Hatch, an analyst at UBS Securities, "Strategically (Heritage Media) is an excellent fit to its direct marketing business."
